scenario.name: SpecterOps, Microsoft ADV210003 & CISA DFIR — AD CS ESC1 SubjectAltName Spoofing & PKINIT Forensics (EID 4886 / 4768)
scenario.overview: Imagine a corporate ID-card print shop that offers one carelessly designed visitor badge template allowing any requester to handwrite whoever they please on the official nameplate line with zero manager approval. A junior clerk spots that sloppy template, types the Chief Executive name onto the application slip, picks up a genuinely embossed executive photo ID straight from the print shop, and exchanges that real badge at the front gate for master keys to the entire company. In this scenario (T1649, SpecterOps, Microsoft ADV210003 & CISA DFIR, AD CS ESC1 SubjectAltName Spoofing & PKINIT Forensics , EID 4886 / 4768), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: eSC1 Vulnerable Certificate Template, then cSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN, then kerberos PKINIT Authentication. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ESC1 Vulnerable Certificate Template, then CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN, then Kerberos PKINIT Authentication, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1649 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: ESC1 Vulnerable Certificate Template Enumeration over LDAP (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT)
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1649 - Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates: ESC1 Discovery)
stages.description: Browsing the print shop public catalog of available ID templates, a low-ranking clerk hunts for one dangerous combination: any ordinary worker can apply, no supervisor signature is required, the badge grants building entry, and the applicant is allowed to type any name they want onto the nameplate. Using Certify.exe find /vulnerable or Certipy, the attacker queries CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration,DC=corp,DC=local and identifies a template ("CorpVPNUser") where Domain Users have Enroll rights, EKU includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), and msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag has bit 0x00000001 (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT) enabled (logged in Network Event 389 with VulnerableTemplate=CorpVPNUser, NameFlagBit=0x00000001 , CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT, ExtendedKeyUsage=1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2 , Client Authentication so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Certify.exe find /vulnerable (which Submits a PKCS#10 / CMC certificate enrollment request , via certreq.exe or ICertRequestD2 to the Enterprise CA specifying an Enrollable template a so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1649 during "ESC1 Vulnerable Certificate Template Enumeration over LDAP , CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). Next, the follow-up artifact LDAP Filter: (&, objectclass=pkicertificatetemplate, msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag:1.2.840.113556.1.4.804:=1) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , LDAP Filter: &, objectclass=pkicertificatetemplate, msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag:1.2.840.11 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1649 during "ESC1 Vulnerable Certificate Template Enumeration over LDAP , CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT" , Using Certify while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Certify.exe find /vulnerable (Querying CN=Certificate Templates) / ⇠#1 RESP 389) from Node ① (#1 Certify.exe / Certipy Host) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CORP-DC01 PKINIT KDC (:88)).

stages.title: Stage 2: CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN (CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1649 - AD CS ESC1 SAN Spoofing & EventID 4886/4887)
stages.description: Filling out an official badge order under their own lowly employee name, the junior clerk neatly writes the Chief Administrator address inside the alternate-identity box. Without pausing for human review, the automated print shop embosses and hands over a cryptographically genuine executive badge while stamping a permanent print-shop log. The low-privileged user (CORP\jdoe) submits a PKCS#10 CSR to CORP-CA01 specifying /altname:Administrator@corp.local. On CORP-CA01, certsrv.exe logs Security EventID 4886 (Certificate Services received a certificate request) and EventID 4887 (Approved and issued a certificate) where Requester="CORP\jdoe" mismatches the issued SubjectAltName="upn=Administrator@corp.local" (and post-KB5014754 logs Microsoft-Windows-CertificationAuthority EID 53/54 if strong mapping is missing) (logged in WinEvent Event 4887 with EventID=4886 , CSR Received / 4887 , Certificate Issued, RequesterAccount=CORP\jdoe , Low-Privileged User, SpoofedSubjectAltName=upn=Administrator@corp.local , Domain Admin, CertificateSerialNumber=61000005C9A18204B19283740000000005C9 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Certify.exe request /ca:CORP-CA01.corp.local\corp-CA /template:CorpVPNUser /altname:Administrator@corp.local (which Submits a PKCS#10 / CMC certificate enrollment request , via certreq.exe or ICertRequestD2 to the Enterprise CA specifying an Enrollable template a so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1649 during "CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN , CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). Next, the follow-up artifact CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887: Requester=CORP\jdoe | SubjectAltName="otherName:Principal Name=Administrator@corp.local" runs (which Submits a PKCS#10 / CMC certificate enrollment request , via certreq.exe or ICertRequestD2 to the Enterprise CA specifying an Enrollable template a so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1649 during "CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN , CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ICertRequestD2::Request Template=CorpVPNUser SAN=Administrator@corp.local / ⇠#2 ACK 4887) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 DCOM ICertRequestD2 RPC), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CORP-DC01 PKINIT KDC (:88)).

Enable Audit Certification Services on all Enterprise CAs (configuring auditfilter 127 via certutil -setreg CA\AuditFilter 127) so EventID 4886 and 4887 log the SubjectAltName field, and alert whenever Requester UPN != SAN UPN.

stages.title: Stage 3: Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash (KDC EventID 4768)
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1649 - PKINIT EventID 4768 & Unpac-the-Hash)
stages.description: Walking up to the central gatehouse with the newly minted executive badge, the clerk trades the photo ID for an official executive master pass and peels the Administrator permanent vault key straight out of the returned pass packet. The attacker converts the issued certificate to a PFX and runs Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /getcredentials. CORP-DC01 validates the certificate via PKINIT (PA-PK-AS-REQ) and logs Security EventID 4768 (A Kerberos authentication ticket , TGT was requested) where TargetUserName=Administrator and CertIssuerName="corp-CA" / CertThumbprint is populated instead of password pre-authentication, while Rubeus decrypts the PAC_CREDENTIAL_INFO structure to recover Administrator’s permanent NTLM hash (logged in WinEvent Event 4768 with EventID=4768 , Kerberos TGT Requested via PKINIT, PreAuthType=16 , PA-PK-AS-REQ SmartCard/Certificate, TargetUserName=Administrator, CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A392817263544556677889900AABB so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /getcredentials /ptt (which executes Active Directory credential harvesting or Kerberos ticket manipulation , Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /get so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1649 during "Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash , KDC EventID 4768" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). Next, the follow-up artifact KDC Security EventID 4768: TargetUserName=Administrator PreAuthType=16 (PA-PK-AS-REQ) CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A... runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1649 during "Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash , KDC EventID 4768" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ PKINIT AS-REQ (PreAuthType=16) for Administrator using CertSerial 61000005C9... / ⇠#3 ACK 4768) from Node ③ (#3 DCOM ICertRequestD2 RPC) to Node ④ (#4 CORP-CA01 (certsrv.exe)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 CORP-DC01 PKINIT KDC (:88)).

keySpecs.value: KDC Security EventID 4768: TargetUserName=Administrator PreAuthType=16 (PA-PK-AS-REQ) CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A...
Unpac-the-Hash: Decrypts PAC_CREDENTIAL_INFO (NTLMCredentialData) using AS-REP session key

Enforce KB5014754 Full Enforcement mode (StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=2) so certificates lacking the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.25.2 Sid-Extension matching the target user objectSid are rejected by the KDC (KDC_ERR_INCONSISTENT_KEY_PURPOSE / EventID 39/41).

steps.plainTitle: CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN (CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887)
steps.storyAnalogy: Filling out an official badge order under their own lowly employee name, the junior clerk neatly writes the Chief Administrator address inside the alternate-identity box. Without pausing for human review, the automated print shop embosses and hands over a cryptographically genuine executive badge while stamping a permanent print-shop log.
steps.simpleExplanation: The low-privileged user (CORP\jdoe) submits a PKCS#10 CSR to CORP-CA01 specifying /altname:Administrator@corp.local. On CORP-CA01, certsrv.exe logs Security EventID 4886 (Certificate Services received a certificate request) and EventID 4887 (Approved and issued a certificate) where Requester="CORP\jdoe" mismatches the issued SubjectAltName="upn=Administrator@corp.local" (and post-KB5014754 logs Microsoft-Windows-CertificationAuthority EID 53/54 if strong mapping is missing) (logged in WinEvent Event 4887 with EventID=4886 , CSR Received / 4887 , Certificate Issued, RequesterAccount=CORP\jdoe , Low-Privileged User, SpoofedSubjectAltName=upn=Administrator@corp.local , Domain Admin, CertificateSerialNumber=61000005C9A18204B19283740000000005C9 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Certify.exe request /ca:CORP-CA01.corp.local\corp-CA /template:CorpVPNUser /altname:Administrator@corp.local (which Submits a PKCS#10 / CMC certificate enrollment request , via certreq.exe or ICertRequestD2 to the Enterprise CA specifying an Enrollable template a so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1649 during "CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN , CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). Next, the follow-up artifact CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887: Requester=CORP\jdoe | SubjectAltName="otherName:Principal Name=Administrator@corp.local" runs (which Submits a PKCS#10 / CMC certificate enrollment request , via certreq.exe or ICertRequestD2 to the Enterprise CA specifying an Enrollable template a so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1649 during "CSR Submission with Spoofed Domain Admin SAN UPN , CA Security EventID 4886 & 4887" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 across the topology from Certify.exe / Certipy Host and DCOM ICertRequestD2 RPC toward CORP-CA01 , certsrv.exe and CA EID 4886/4887 & KDC 4768.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in WinEvent Event 4887 (recording EventID=4886 , CSR Received / 4887 , Certificate Issued, RequesterAccount=CORP\jdoe , Low-Privileged User, SpoofedSubjectAltName=upn=Administrator@corp.local , Domain Admin, CertificateSerialNumber=61000005C9A18204B19283740000000005C9 under T1649): Enable Audit Certification Services on all Enterprise CAs (configuring auditfilter 127 via certutil -setreg CA\AuditFilter 127) so EventID 4886 and 4887 log the SubjectAltName field, and alert whenever Requester UPN != SAN UPN.

steps.plainTitle: Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash (KDC EventID 4768)
steps.storyAnalogy: Walking up to the central gatehouse with the newly minted executive badge, the clerk trades the photo ID for an official executive master pass and peels the Administrator permanent vault key straight out of the returned pass packet.
steps.simpleExplanation: The attacker converts the issued certificate to a PFX and runs Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /getcredentials. CORP-DC01 validates the certificate via PKINIT (PA-PK-AS-REQ) and logs Security EventID 4768 (A Kerberos authentication ticket , TGT was requested) where TargetUserName=Administrator and CertIssuerName="corp-CA" / CertThumbprint is populated instead of password pre-authentication, while Rubeus decrypts the PAC_CREDENTIAL_INFO structure to recover Administrator’s permanent NTLM hash (logged in WinEvent Event 4768 with EventID=4768 , Kerberos TGT Requested via PKINIT, PreAuthType=16 , PA-PK-AS-REQ SmartCard/Certificate, TargetUserName=Administrator, CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A392817263544556677889900AABB so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /getcredentials /ptt (which executes Active Directory credential harvesting or Kerberos ticket manipulation , Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Administrator /certificate:admin.pfx /get so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1649 during "Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash , KDC EventID 4768" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline). Next, the follow-up artifact KDC Security EventID 4768: TargetUserName=Administrator PreAuthType=16 (PA-PK-AS-REQ) CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A... runs (which Constructs or requests Kerberos AS-REQ , EventID 4768 or TGS-REQ , EventID 4769 tickets against the Key Distribution Center , KDC, specifying custo so that compromises Active Directory authentication and service ticket cryptography , T1649 during "Kerberos PKINIT Authentication & NT Hash Extraction via Unpac-the-Hash , KDC EventID 4768" to escalate domain privileges or crack service account credentials offline).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 across the topology from Certify.exe / Certipy Host and DCOM ICertRequestD2 RPC toward CORP-CA01 , certsrv.exe and CA EID 4886/4887 & KDC 4768.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in WinEvent Event 4768 (recording EventID=4768 , Kerberos TGT Requested via PKINIT, PreAuthType=16 , PA-PK-AS-REQ SmartCard/Certificate, TargetUserName=Administrator, CertThumbprint=9F8E7D6C5B4A392817263544556677889900AABB under T1649): Enforce KB5014754 Full Enforcement mode (StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=2) so certificates lacking the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.25.2 Sid-Extension matching the target user objectSid are rejected by the KDC (KDC_ERR_INCONSISTENT_KEY_PURPOSE / EventID 39/41).
